## Submission
TMP Architecture, Inc., 1191 West Square Lake Road, Bloomfield Hills, Michigan 48302 (248.338.4561), responded to Troy School District Bid 9918 for Pre-Bond Architect/Engineer Services. Cover page dated February 3, 2021; transmittal letter dated February 1, 2021 to Mr. Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098, signed by Gail A. Allevato, CPSM, President, and John J. Castellana, FAIA, REFP, Chairman. The document is a preface plus seven sections answering ten numbered RFP questions.

## Proposed team
| Firm | Discipline | Named leads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TMP Architecture | Architecture, planning, campaign | Gail Allevato, John Castellana, John Waldrop |
| Barton Malow | Construction manager | Mike Stoback, Larry Bukowski, Jeff Atkins |
| Peter Basso Associates | Mechanical & electrical | Steven V. Mrak, Gregory J. Ziegler |
| PEA Group | Civil engineering | James Butler |
| Counsilman-Hunsaker | Pool consultant | Carl Nylander, PE |
| Sinclair Recreation, LLC | Playground consultant | Matt Campanella |

Other TMP staff named: Danielle O'Grady, David W. Larson, Danielle O'Neal, Thomas Barber, Franco Antonnicola, Stacey Mazzara, Keri Seeney, Nicollette N. Cardwell, Anna McDevitt and Jason Hynes. Specialists offered if required include Foresite Design, William A. Kibbe & Associates, CMTA, Inc., E.F. Whitney, BAi, LLC and Schuler Shook.

## Firm credentials
TMP was founded in 1959, employs over 85 professionals and reports more than 6,000 K-12 projects. Its Interior Design Group is 10 professionals with a combined total of 140 years of K-12 experience; an Educational Research and Development Committee was formed in 2020. Over the past 10 years TMP claims more than $5 billion in bond programs with 90% passing on the first attempt. Its relationship with Barton Malow spans four decades and 600+ K-12 projects, with Peter Basso Associates almost three decades and 1,600+ projects, and with PEA Group 150+ projects.

## Bond formation plan
Phases run Discovery, Exploration and Recommendation: kickoff March 2021 (2 weeks); facilities and program definition March–August 2021 (6 months); visioning June–July 2021 (8 weeks); steering committee kickoff October 2021; concept options Oct 2021–Feb 2022 (5 months); community engagement March–April 2022 (2 months); district bond plan May 2022 (1 month); bond application June–July 2022 (1 month); campaign June–Nov 2022 (3-6 months); anticipated election day Nov 8, 2022. A Department of Treasury meeting is set for June 2022 with a 30 day formal review in July, and the Board would call the election late July or early August, 12 weeks prior. An optional market survey is priced at 4-6 weeks and $15K-$20K.

## Fee proposal
| Work scope | Hours |
| --- | --- |
| Kickoff with District Leadership | 24 |
| Visioning Sessions | 160 |
| Facility Assessments | 550 |
| Program Assessments | 320 |
| Discovery / Exploration with Steering Group | 400 |
| Community Engagement | 80 |
| Develop District Bond Plan | 240 |
| Bond Application | 80 |
| Bond Campaign | 480 |
| Sub-Total | 2,334 |
| Note 1 deduction | 275 |
| Adjusted Total | 2059 |

Blended hourly rate at direct cost $68.75 / hr.; stipulated sum $141,556.25. An independent survey such as EPIC MRA would be a reimbursable or direct cost. If TMP and Barton Malow are retained through implementation, the full stipulated amount is credited to the ultimate negotiated professional fees.

## References
South Redford School District (Brian Galdes, 313.535.4000), Jackson Public Schools (Jeff Beal, 517.841.2201), Northville Public Schools (Mary Kay Gallagher, 248.344.3508), Hartland Consolidated Schools (Chuck Hughes, 810.626.2100), School District of the City of Saginaw (Dr. Ramont M. Roberts, 989.399.6501) and Troy School District (Kerry Birmingham, 248.823.4035).
2021_175_8_f_tmp_response_to_troy_school.verbose:
TMP Architecture, Inc. prepared this response to the Troy School District Request for Proposals, Bid 9918, Pre-Bond Architect/Engineer Services. The cover page carries the date February 3, 2021; the transmittal letter is dated February 1, 2021 and addressed to Mr. Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098. It is signed by Gail A. Allevato, CPSM, President, and John J. Castellana, FAIA, REFP, Chairman. TMP Architecture Inc. is at 1191 West Square Lake Road, Bloomfield Hills, Michigan 48302 (PH 248.338.4561, FX 248.338.0223), with a second office at 259 E. Michigan Ave., Suite 107, Kalamazoo, MI 49007 (269.327.0077).

ORGANIZATION. The table of contents lists a Preface, "Strength, Growth & Benefit," then seven sections keyed to ten RFP questions: Invested in Life Long Learning, Educational Planners at Heart, Flash Drive Deliverables, Communicating For Success, Creating your Vision, Celebrating Success and Fee Proposal.

FIRM PROFILE. TMP was founded in 1959 and describes itself as a firm of over 85 professionals that has completed over 6,000 projects for primary and secondary school clients. The preface cites eight years of day-to-day work in the District since the start of Troy's 2013 Bond, an Educational Research and Development Committee formed in 2020, and more than $5 billion in bond programs over the past 10 years with 90% passing on the first attempt. TMP's Interior Design Group is described as 10 professionals with a combined total of 140 years of recent K-12 experience. A sample furniture listing for the Royal Oak High School Learning Commons (TMP Project No. 16022, May 4, 2016) prices Priority 1 Hearth at a subtotal of $16,400 with 10% contingency $1,640 for $18,040; Priority 2 Learning Pod 2 at $14,550 plus $1,455 for $16,005; Priority 2A Group Room at $12,300 plus $1,230 for $13,530; Priority 2B Collaboration Station Lab at $40,450 plus $4,045 for $44,495; and Priority 3 Learning Pod 1 at $14,050.

PARTNER FIRMS. Barton Malow is proposed as construction manager, with more than 1,000 team members across 14 offices; it began technology services in 1993, formalized its Technology Services group in 1997, and reports over $500,000,000 in K-12 technology projects. TMP's relationship with Barton Malow spans four decades and 600+ K-12 projects. Peter Basso Associates provides mechanical and electrical engineering, with a TMP relationship of almost three decades and 1,600+ projects and nearly 1,000 K-12 projects together since the first in 1995. PEA Group, in practice since 1947, provides civil engineering across almost three decades and 150+ projects with TMP. Counsilman-Hunsaker (pool consultant) has more than 45 years of aquatic work and over 30 projects with TMP. Sinclair Recreation, LLC was started by Diane and Richard Sinclair on April 1st of 2003 after a combined 53 years with the local GameTime representative and has completed an estimated 250 supervisions since 2003; GameTime has been committed to play since 1929 from a 400,000 square foot facility on 81 acres. Additional specialists are Foresite Design, Inc. (athletic fields, over 50 projects with TMP); William A. Kibbe & Associates, Inc. (structural, founded in Saginaw, Michigan in 1981, over 40 projects with TMP); CMTA, Inc. (zero energy and MEP, currently working with TMP at Ann Arbor Public Schools); E.F. Whitney, Inc. (food service, a self-certified Women Based Enterprise, over 450 projects with TMP); BAi, LLC (acoustics, founded 1935, over 1,130 Pre K-12 projects, over 190 projects with TMP); and Schuler Shook (theater, founded 1986 by Duane Schuler and Robert Shook).

PASSAGE-RATE CHART. Entries include Ann Arbor Public Schools 2019 Bond $1 B PASS; Walled Lake Consolidated Schools 2019 Bond $318 M PASS; Plymouth-Canton Schools 2020 Bond $275 M PASS; Novi Community Schools 2019 Bond $185 M PASS; Huron Valley Schools 2019 Bond $182 M PASS; Wayne-Westland School District 2018 Bond $158 M PASS; Farmington Public Schools 2015 Bond $131.5 M PASS; East China School District 2020 Bond $112.9 M PASS; Northville Public Schools 2017 Bond $104.8 M PASS; Saginaw Public School District 2020 Bond $99.5 M PASS; Jackson Public Schools 2018 Bond $89.5 M PASS; South Redford School District 2022 Bond $79.9 M TBD; Royal Oak Schools 2017 Bond $59.9 M PASS; and Troy School District 2017 10 yr. Sinking Fund $36 M PASS.

TEAM. Assignments are Gail A. Allevato, Project Executive/Campaign Leader; John Castellana, Educational Planning/Design Leader; John Waldrop, AIA, LEED AP, Project Manager/Assessment Leader; Danielle O'Grady, IIDA, NCIDQ, and David W. Larson, AIA, Program Assessment and Visioning; Thomas Barber, AIA, Danielle O'Neal, AIA, NCARB, and Franco Antonnicola, Assessment Team; Stacey Mazzara and Keri Seeney, NCIDQ, Program Assessment Team; Nicollette N. Cardwell, Campaign Leader; Anna McDevitt and Jason Hynes, Campaign Team. Barton Malow supplies Mike Stoback, Larry Bukowski and Jeff Atkins; Peter Basso Associates supplies Steven V. Mrak, PE, MBA, and Gregory J. Ziegler, FE; PEA Group supplies James Butler; Counsilman-Hunsaker supplies Carl Nylander, PE. The organizational chart names Rob Carson and Michelle Kerns in the owner's representative, TSD director of operations and maintenance, and facilities liaison roles; the Board of Education as Karl Schmidt, Dr. Nicole Wilson, Gary Hauff, Vital Anne, Steve Gottlieb, Elizabeth Hammond and Dr. Nancy Philippart; and Central Office Administration as Dr. Richard Machesky, Kerry Birmingham, Jessica Carrier, Christine DiPilato, Kristine Griffor, Jordan Harris and Rick West.

BIOGRAPHIES. Allevato holds a Bachelor of Science in Marketing and Human Resource Management from Wayne State University, 1984, and CPSM certification, 1993; she joined TMP in 1986, became Director of Marketing in 1987, Senior Vice President in 2004, Chief Marketing Officer in 2006 and the sixth President of TMP in 2018, and has lived in Troy since 1995. Castellana holds a Master of Architecture from the University of Illinois, 1972, and a Bachelor of Architecture from Kent State University, 1971, received the AIA Michigan Gold Medal in 2016 and the AIA Detroit Gold Medal in 2000, entered the AIA College of Fellows in 1988 and was named its Chancellor in 2021, and cites a 48 year career. Waldrop holds a Master of Architecture from the University of Michigan, 1991, with 33 years in the industry and 27 years as a registered architect. Stoback has 33 years of experience, worked on Troy High School in 1988, dates the Barton Malow partnership to a 1985 planning effort and a 35 year relationship, and notes Barton Malow's 1988 sponsorship of the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence. Others include Bukowski (15 years, LEED AP BD+C, Troy resident), Atkins (27 years), Larson (Kent State University, 1975; over 43 years, 37 with TMP), Barber (Carleton University, 1978; over 36 years, 16 with TMP), Seeney (NCIDQ 2018), Cardwell (San Diego State University, 2013), McDevitt (joined TMP July 2020), Ziegler (35 years) and Nylander (Georgia Institute of Technology, 2003).

DELIVERABLES AND CASE STUDIES. Flash drive samples cover Facilities Assessment books, Program Assessments, Recommendation Books and Campaign Materials for Huron Valley Schools, South Redford School District, Hartland Consolidated Schools, Tecumseh Public Schools, Jackson Public Schools, Ann Arbor Public Schools and Troy School District. A Jackson Public Schools Bennett Elementary School dashboard shows Building Exterior 946,634, Plumbing 357,500, Electrical 340,034, Mechanical 214,500, Classrooms 182,000, Site 181,350 and Code Issues 67,080, with year totals of 1,893,424.00, 510,835.00 and 264,243.85 plus 8,294.00 not bondable, and a total of all categories of 2,676,796.85; an electrical worksheet dated June 6, 2017 for the Middle School at Parkside totals $1,922,655. A Northville Facility Assessment Study dated February 2, 2015 describes Amerman Elementary School at 847 North Center Street, 69,564 gross square feet on a 10.2 acre site, built 1955 with additions in 1957, 1969, 1999 and 2003, with deficiency values of $472,743, $1,277,165 and $788,299. Case studies cover Jackson Public Schools' $86.74 million May 2018 bond, which passed with 61% community support and a 2.95 mill increase; Northville's $104.85 million November 2017 zero-tax-increase bond, which passed by nearly a 2 to 1 margin; Troy School District's $125 million November 5, 2013 bond, which passed 70/30, maintained the existing 4.7 mill debt levy and was to be issued in multiple series over seven (7) years for Safety and Security, Technology, Facilities and Sites, Instructional Equipment and Buses; and Saginaw Public Schools' November 3, 2020 bond, headed as $99.9M and described as a $99.5 million proposal with a 7 mill increase and high school consolidation, run entirely virtually. Campaign samples also include Novi's $185 million proposal (7.00 current, 6.75 projected), Walled Lake's May 7, 2019 $316 million program, East China's March 10, 2020 $112.9 million proposal, Huron Valley's $182M bond and Ann Arbor's $1B program.

REFERENCES AND FEE. References are South Redford School District (Mr. Brian Galdes, 313.535.4000), Jackson Public Schools (Mr. Jeff Beal, 517.841.2201), Northville Public Schools (Ms. Mary Kay Gallagher, 248.344.3508), Hartland Consolidated Schools (Mr. Chuck Hughes, 810.626.2100), School District of the City of Saginaw (Dr. Ramont M. Roberts, Ph.D., 989.399.6501) and Troy School District (Ms. Kerry Birmingham, 248.823.4035). The fee proposal estimates Kickoff 24 hours, Visioning Sessions 160 hours, Facility Assessments 550 hours, Program Assessments 320 hours, Discovery/Exploration with Steering Group 400 hours, Community Engagement 80 hours, Develop District Bond Plan 240 hours, Bond Application 80 hours and Bond Campaign 480 hours for a sub-total of 2,334 hours, less a note-1 deduction of 275 hours, for an adjusted total of 2059 hours. At a blended hourly rate at direct cost of $68.75 / hr., the stipulated sum is $141,556.25. An independent survey such as EPIC MRA would be a reimbursable or direct cost to the District, and if the TMP and Barton Malow team is retained through implementation the full stipulated amount would be credited to the ultimate negotiated professional fees. The plan assumes a November 2022 election date, updates the 2018 Facilities Assessment of all District buildings, and anticipates election day Nov 8, 2022 with a Treasury meeting in June 2022, a 30 day formal review in July, and a Board call for election late July or early August, 12 weeks prior to the election. An optional professional market survey is priced at 4-6 weeks and $15K-$20K.
